fx.fx_commentary: The Canadian dollar fell to 0.7198 CAD/USD (1.3893 USD/CAD) on March 30 — down 1.85% month-over-month to a two-month low — the move occurred against the backdrop of the 125–150 basis point spread between the Federal Reserve's 3.50–3.75% target and the Bank of Canada's 2.25% policy rate.1 Year-over-year, the loonie is up 2.61% against the US dollar.1 The euro traded at 1.1460 EUR/USD amid geopolitical uncertainty.2 The database tracks 653 projects in trade-exposed sectors (manufacturing, agriculture, transport logistics) where FX movements directly affect input costs or export revenue.3

yieldCurve.yield_commentary: The Government of Canada yield curve maintained a normal shape in the week ending March 30, with the 2–10 year spread at 63 basis points — the 10-year yield stood at 3.58% against the 2-year at 2.95%.4 Across the full curve: the 3-month at 2.28%, the 1-year at 2.55%, the 5-year at 3.18%, the 20-year at 3.85%, and the 30-year at 3.94%.4 Year-over-year, the belly and long end rose: the 2-year is up 33 basis points from 2.62%, the 10-year up 36 basis points from 3.22%, while the 3-month fell 122 basis points from 3.50% as the Bank of Canada completed seven consecutive cuts from the June 2024 peak of 5.00%.45 The database tracks 2,739 projects in proposed or approved status in rate-sensitive sectors, including 211 residential and 68 commercial-mixed projects.3
